title: CRASH-051: std call user call stack zval args zval_dtor frees retained value suar (stack-use-after-return)
live_proof: measured, not asserted: our native ASan build of the pinned 5.0.0 tarball (p12, gcc 15.2.0, libasan from gcc 15, 2026-10-27) reports ASAN:stack-use-after-return at Zend/zend_execute.c:59 in zend_pzval_lock_func when trigger.php runs; the corpus records the fix as php-src 235e6c0afe1d, which postdates the release, and names the defect at Zend/zend_object_handlers.c:524 (+ :542, :587-588)
fidelity: the corpus's own trigger script, run through the real interpreter (PHP's cli SAPI, ext/standard only, the port's 145 translation units) rather than reduced to a C model. What it does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it. The pristine build completes it natively, so an arm that completes it saw nothing.

virtual-malloc.oracle: the case on the virtual profile with the seam present but returning every freed block's loan, so only musl mallocng revokes, per BLOCK, when PHP's cache hands a block back to free(): a fault at the ASan site, or the trigger ends and this arm did not see it (tools/arms.json php-real-block)

virtual-nested-pools.oracle: the same image with the allocator seam retiring the payload at EVERY _efree, cache-absorbed or not, and re-deriving it under a fresh node when the cache hands the block to its next tenant: a fault at the ASan site, or the trigger ends and this arm did not see it (php-real-object)

virtual-nested-exact.oracle: virtual-nested-pools with each payload bounded to the caller's request instead of REAL_SIZE(n): the arm that can see a defect inside PHP's own rounding slack (php-real-exact)

status: built 2026-10-27 from the corpus and our native oracle; not yet run on the virtual profile from this corpus
note: population: asan-blind -- ASan reports it only with PHP's allocator patched (cache off, no 8-byte rounding); with zend_alloc.c as shipped the run reads OK, so emalloc's cache or rounding hides it from any detector at free(). Collected by the corpus as history-5.x (historical-known, confidence high).
